answer: Each identity pays a small per-epoch burn to stay active, like a falcon that must beat its wings to stay airborne. A monitoring layer watches for identities whose liveness signals move in lockstep — that correlation betrays the fable of one actor pretending to be a crowd. When such a cluster is flagged, its bonds freeze until every member completes fresh, independently-assigned verification work; clones that cannot each do the task burn out. An attacker must fund and operate every clone continuously, so a sybil army stays costly to keep alive while an honest identity pays a trivial fee.
